svg.title: The bread before His face
svg.desc: A one-minute comic in 5 panels. Panel 1 (Matthew 12:1-2): Jesus walks through a field with two disciples, who pluck grain; two authorities point at them. Caption: "On a Sabbath Jesus went through the grainfields. His disciples were hungry and began to pluck heads of grain and eat." An authority says: "Look, your disciples are doing what is not lawful to do on the Sabbath." Panel 2 (Matthew 12:3): Jesus answers the authorities. Jesus says: "Have you not read what David did when he was hungry?" Panel 3 (Matthew 12:4): Jesus goes on, pointing back. Jesus says: "He ate the bread of the Presence, which only the priests could eat." Panel 4 (1 Samuel 21:1-6), a flashback: at Nob the priest holds out a loaf to David. Caption: "Earlier: David, fleeing from Saul, came hungry to Ahimelech the priest at Nob. The only bread was the bread removed from before the LORD." A priest says: "I have no common bread on hand, but there is holy bread." Panel 5 (Matthew 12:6-8): Jesus faces the authorities; the disciples stand behind Him. Jesus says: "Something greater than the temple is here. I desire mercy, and not sacrifice." The point: The bread set out before God's face fed a hungry man, and the One greater than the temple says God desires mercy, so you can come to Him in your need (Matthew 12:6-7).
svg.text: Matthew 12 and 1 Samuel 21 in one minute

g.text: On a Sabbath Jesus went through the
grainfields. His disciples were hungry and
began to pluck heads of grain and eat.
Earlier: David, fleeing from Saul, came hungry
to Ahimelech the priest at Nob. The only bread
was the bread removed from before the LORD.

svg.text: The bread set out before God's face fed a hungry man, and
the One greater than the temple says God desires mercy,
so you can come to Him in your need (Matthew 12:6-7).
Each panel names its verses; “condensed” marks words shortened from the ESV.
